newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: UNHCR's Ogata slams "international neglect" of Zaire.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR's Ogata slams "international neglect" of Zaire.

text.p: The head of the U.N.'s refugee agency on Tuesday slammed the international community over the crisis in Zaire and called for an African rapid reaction force to intervene in conflicts.
U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata said in a speech to South Africa's parliament that the crisis in Zaire was partly a result of the failure of the international community.

"The absence of a convergence of interests and views among the major powers also results in preventing this drama from receiving the international attention and determination it deserves for solution," Ogata said.

Analysts said she was referring to reported tension between the United States and France over the diplomatic spoils in Central Africa, a tussle some have blamed for the lack of pressure to end the fighting, in which rebels have seized about a quarter of Zaire.
Ogata said she was dismayed that a military force proposed for Central Africa last year had not been formed.
"Let me not hide my disappointment about the cancellation of the multinational force that had been authorised by the Security Council to come to the rescue of refugees in Zaire," she said.

"I would therefore like to use this opportunity to appeal to you to support the creation of an African rapid reaction capability which would also have the functions of demobilisation and separation of armed elements."

When Rwandan refugees returned home from Zaire late last year the intervention force was cancelled although thousands remained behind in the jungle. Aid workers are now trying to help those left behind as the conflict in Zaire escalates.
Many of the refugees in Zaire are ethnic Hutus believed to have been involved in genocide in Rwanda in 1994, when up to a million ethnic Tutsis and moderate Hutus were slaughtered.
Ogata said that in the absence of outside intervention, a ceasefire was needed for aid agencies to tend to their needs.

"The failure of asylum countries and the international community to separate the former military and people who committed genocide from the innocent refugees in the Rwandan refugee camps has contributed considerably to the spreading of conflict to Zaire," she added.
Ogata praised South Africa for its efforts to broker a truce between forces of President Mobutu Sese Seko and the followers of rebel leader Laurent Kabila, who started their campaign last October.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan told President Nelson Mandela during a visit to South Africa last week that he was in favour of a proposed rapid reaction unit for Africa.
Mandela reaffirmed that he was opposed to an African force managed in any way by Western countries such as the United States, who first proposed the idea last year.
"That initiative must come from Africa," he said.
